bundle.author: delegate-gp-bot
bundle.title: ENG-11245: tolerate transient Vercel errors while polling registrar order
bundle.body:
Why: alert [Win] Route errors on POST /v1/domains/purchase (2026-10-09 ~18:05Z). The purchase succeeded at Vercel (order created), then the first getOrder poll returned a 502 from Vercel. assertRegistrarOrderCompleted threw, the domain was set inactive, and the user's retry hit 409 'no longer available' for the domain they had just bought.

Fix: while polling, a Vercel 5xx/429 is a non-terminal poll and is retried on the normal interval; the last attempt and non-transient errors still throw.

Unrelated to the voter-density alert at the same minute: no election-api errors in the window; failure is a Vercel upstream 502.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes domain purchase completion behavior on Vercel API failures; incorrect classification could delay failure or mask real errors, but scope is limited to registrar order polling.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a production failure where a successful Vercel registrar purchase could still fail registration when the first `getRegistrarOrder` poll returned a transient upstream error (e.g. 502), which marked the domain **inactive** and left the user unable to retry.
> 
> Adds `isVercelTransientError` on `VercelService` (Vercel **5xx** and **429**). **`assertRegistrarOrderCompleted`** now catches those errors during polling, waits the existing interval, and retries instead of aborting—non-transient errors and the final poll attempt still throw. A unit test covers retry-after-transient-error without setting the domain inactive.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f2bc49315f79776fe6df218f70d190bbca08d6a4. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

findings.body:
**Last-attempt transient error still strands the purchase.**

When `attempt === REGISTRAR_ORDER_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS` and Vercel returns a transient 5xx, the guard `attempt < REGISTRAR_ORDER_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS` is false, so the raw `VercelError` is re-thrown. It propagates to the outer catch at line 1385, which unconditionally sets `status: DomainStatus.inactive` — the same stranded-purchase scenario the PR is designed to prevent.

Removing only the `attempt <` guard doesn't fully help either: the loop would exit and the timeout throw at line 1479 still reaches the same outer catch. The deeper fix is either (a) removing the attempt guard here **and** having the outer catch distinguish transient-poll-exhaustion from real failures (so it doesn't mark inactive when all polls were transient), or (b) accepting one extra retry by dropping the guard, which at least gives the final poll a chance to succeed rather than failing immediately on the transient error.

(Falsification check: the outer catch at lines 1385–1397 has no transient-error guard — it calls `model.update({ status: DomainStatus.inactive })` unconditionally for all exceptions from `assertRegistrarOrderCompleted`.)

output.summary: This PR adds transient-error tolerance (5xx/429) to the Vercel registrar-order polling loop in `assertRegistrarOrderCompleted`, preventing a confirmed production bug where a Vercel 502 on the first poll marked a successfully purchased domain as inactive. The scout flagged three areas: (1) the transient-error guard excludes the final poll attempt, (2) test coverage for `isVercelTransientError` itself, and (3) non-`VercelError` network failures. Deep review confirmed that items 2 and 3 are not blockers — the test correctly isolates the retry logic with standard mocking, and the scope to `VercelError` matches the observed failure. Item 1 is a medium-confidence concern: a transient error on the last attempt still throws raw and triggers the outer catch's unconditional `inactive` marking, preserving the stranded-purchase risk in that edge case. The human reviewer should confirm whether the polling budget (attempt count × interval) is generous enough that exhausting all attempts on transient errors is unlikely in practice.
